00:11 area probability density

12 runs, 1,020,000 initial candidates. 86.5% of pooled probability lies between 35°S and 38°S; 12.5% lies farther north.

Sampling status when generated: sampling completed. This report includes 1,020,000 of the planned 1,020,000 initial candidates. Refresh the report to see newly completed batches.

A provisional PDF under the declared flight and evidence conditions. Independent runs show sampling variation; a fixed five-point threshold is not used to withhold the estimate.

Altitude is a distribution, including at 00:11

35,000 ft is only the altitude of the dashed reference line on the map. Each candidate retains its own altitude in the SATCOM calculation and in the area PDF. The model allows nominal levels from 25,000 to 43,000 ft and up to 2 altitude changes after 18:25.

The weighted median terminal altitude is 37,000 ft; the 5th–95th percentiles are 32,000–42,000 ft. These are calculated results under the model, not observed altitudes.

How trajectory complexity relates to latitude

The first graphic shows the turn, Mach and altitude change counts within each 2.5° latitude bin. Its top panel shows the probability assigned to each bin, so an extremely rare tail is not mistaken for a major part of the estimate. The second shows the latitude distribution after conditioning on each count separately. These comparisons describe the current prior and manoeuvre caps; increasing the caps is a separate sensitivity calculation.

What changed as the ensemble grew?

Compared with the original 3 runs combined, the additional runs have maximum latitude/longitude cumulative differences of 6.8/10.8 percentage points. Combining all 12 moves the original curves by 5.2/8.3 points.

Pooling reduces the influence of each new run mechanically. Small successive changes alone do not prove convergence; the separate groups below provide a comparison without shared particles.

How the runs are combined

Each run retains its candidate weights. The main estimate adds the equal-effort runs’ unnormalized probability measures and then normalizes their sum. Each run therefore contributes in proportion to its estimated normalizing constant.

An equal-run average gives 87.5% in 35–38°S; the maximum coordinate-CDF difference from the main pooling is 1.1 points.

Andrieu, Doucet and Holenstein (2010), §4–5 and p. 298 establishes the SMC normalizer identities under its stated assumptions. This pooling is the ratio of sums of saved unnormalized estimates. A finite ratio is not claimed to be unbiased, and the paper does not establish convergence of this implementation.

Conditions, interpretation and reproducibility

The target allows at most 4 turn starts, 2 Mach starts and 2 altitude starts after 18:25:34. 5 navigation families remain in the prior. Nominal Mach 0.73–0.84 and altitude 25,000–43,000 ft are model conditions; small cruise fluctuations are additional. BTO/BFO through 00:10:59 and the declared fuel compatibility are enabled. The vertical-speed contribution to BFO is disabled in this frozen configuration. The fuel continuation assumes exhaustion between 00:15 and 00:19 and gives an outer 0.2–1.9 tonne usable-fuel envelope. This uses Martin/BSM LRC coefficients plus a declared extension; full performance and fuel calibration remain incomplete.

The 1,020,000 initial candidates evolve through resampling, so their descendants are correlated. Pooling 12 runs is different from running one interacting filter with 1,020,000 particles. Replication helps assess sampling variation but does not establish that all feasible routes were explored, or that these conditional probabilities represent all physical uncertainty.

End-of-flight, antenna gain, ocean drift, hydroacoustics, Pleiades, WSPR and searched-area evidence are not enabled in this estimate.

The map is an unsmoothed weighted histogram on a WGS84 equal-area grid. All sample mass is retained in the grid; each figure states the mass inside its displayed frame. Altitude and across-arc position spread are retained.

The output directory includes summary.json, pooled-particles.csv, area-density-5km.csv/npz and SVG/PDF/PNG figures. Its README gives one command to regenerate them without running the filter.
